Truganini.fact: In July the party set out on another expedition to locate the remaining Tarkiner. While the expedition party eventually located most of the Tarkiner, all of their adults quickly died after being brought to Sarah Island.

Truganini.fact: By April, they had located 20 more Aboriginal people.

Truganini.question: The conditions at Wybalenna were poor; of the 300 Aboriginal Tasmanians who had surrendered to Robinson since _____, just 112 were alive at Wybalenna in 1835

Truganini.fact: By 1840, Robinson had decided he no longer had any use for the Tasmanians, and requested that arrangements be made to send them back to Wybalenna.

Truganini.fact: In 1841, while arrangements were still being made for their return to Tasmania, Truganini abandoned her husband Woureddy and ran away with Maulboyheenner.

Truganini.fact: They were soon joined by Peevay and two other Tasmanian women called Plorenernoopner and Maytepueminer, and the five of them set out for Westernport Bay to search for Maytepueminer's husband Lacklay.

Truganini.fact: While being pursued by an armed search party assembled by Watson, Maulboyheenner and Peevay shot and beat to death two whalers they had mistaken for members of Watson's party.

Truganini.fact: After the residents sent petitions to Queen Victoria and to the colony's governor to protest their treatment, the colonial secretary decided in May 1847 that the Wybalenna settlement should be disestablished. Truganini.fact: Truganini's only remaining friend and clanswoman, Dray, died in 1861, leaving Truganini alone in her hut while Lanne was absent on whaling expeditions.
